title: Attribution pipeline for schema-related quality shifts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a reproducible pipeline that attributes observed regressions in structured outputs (JSON/typed responses) to specific model/config changes made during rollouts. Current monitors flag schema violations and end-to-end quality drops, but owners spend manual effort triaging whether a change in model weights, temperature, sampling, quantization profile, or tokenization caused the shift. This ticket implements an attribution layer that: 1) collects per-change diffs (model version, config deltas, compilation flags), 2) computes per-field and per-example impact scores using paired sample diffs and weighted eval metrics, 3) correlates temporal signals with rollout events and infra incidents, and 4) produces ranked candidate root causes with confidence estimates and suggested mitigations (rollback, tweak config, use fallback model). The pipeline should integrate with existing eval harness and rollout metadata, expose explanations in Console (recently-failed canary -> likely-cause), and emit structured alerts for automated incident playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: every rollout event includes a change bundle id that the pipeline can query
Attribution output: for a detected regression, pipeline returns a ranked list of up to 5 change candidates with an "attribution_score" and top-3 supporting examples
Per-field delta: compute delta metrics (precision/recall/format-fidelity) per JSON field and surface in the dashboard
Integration: Console shows the top candidate with a one-click create-incident action linking to the PR/Diff and suggested mitigation
Performance: end-to-end attribution run for a canary window (1k examples) completes under 15 minutes on standard infra
Confidence gating: false-positive rate on a labeled validation set <= 8%
design_considerations: Use paired-sample evaluation when available (same prompts sent to old and new configs). Fall back to statistical matching if paired samples missing.

Attribution score combines effect size (per-field metric delta), coverage (fraction of affected examples), and config significance (majority-weighted by semantic importance of change, e.g., model weight upgrade > temperature tweak).
Support both hosted and dedicated rollout metadata; rollout events include model_hash, quant_profile, tokenizer_version, sampling_params, and target_pool.
Allow operator overrides: ability to pin which diff types count more in the score for a given project.
Privacy: sample examples used in attribution must be masked if flagged by data-sensitivity labels and obey KMS access controls.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (MVP): offline batch correlator that runs after canary window closes and writes attribution artifacts to S3 + index in Postgres
Phase 2: near-real-time stream-based correlator for sliding windows and live alerts
Core components: change-collector (ingests rollout metadata), diff-evaluator (computes per-field deltas), correlator (temporal association + causal heuristics), reporter (dashboard + alert emitter)
Leverage existing structured-output eval suite (ENG-34127/ENG-36521) for the diff-evaluator; add new metrics for JSON shape stability and extraneous-field rate
Create a lightweight explainer that extracts top example pairs illustrating the regression for on-call review
Add unit/integration tests that replay historical rollouts where root cause is known (sourced from incident logs)
testing_plan: Synthetic regression corpus: create controlled diffs (temperature, quant, tokenization) and validate that attribution ranks the injected change first >= 90% of the time
Backfill test: run pipeline against last 12 production rollouts and compare generated candidates to postmortem conclusions for precision/recall
Canary run: enable for a low-traffic project for 2 weeks, collect operator feedback, and measure noise rate
Load test: ensure 1k-example attribution completes < 15 minutes on staging cluster; benchmark memory/CPU footprint
